text:
Maya: Heads-up — noticed the canary for the rollout to v2 is showing a sustained 0.9% error rate vs baseline 0.1% but alert didn't fire. digging into the dashboard now.
Kevin: hmm, is the alert rule bound to absolute error rate or relative change?
Maya: looks like current alert is absolute > 1% over 5m. Canary hit 0.9% so it silently misses.
Olivia: that's by design historically but we should have a relative delta guard for canaries. 0.8->0.9 is a 12% relative increase.
Ravi: agree. We also need a min traffic threshold. small sample noise during rollouts triggers noise. For canaries use min_requests=500 over window.
Maya: proposal: dual-guard: require either absolute threshold OR (relative > X% AND p-value < 0.05 AND min_traffic). Also add a short cooldown to avoid flapping.
Kevin: can we express that in our existing alert DSL? current rule is simple prometheus expr + alertmanager. might need a lightweight evaluation service for canary heuristics.
Olivia: sketch of SQL-ish slice test for attribution:
```sql
SELECT slice_id, count(*) as n, avg(latency) as p50, sum(error) as errors,
       errors::float / n as error_rate
FROM requests
WHERE deployment = 'canary-v2' OR deployment = 'baseline'
GROUP BY slice_id
HAVING n > 100
ORDER BY error_rate DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Maya: exactly — want the slice explorer to surface the top diverging slices and show sample traces inline.
signal-bot: [automated] Canary snapshot recorded: canary:v2 traffic=1200 baseline=4800 p50_delta=+8% error_delta=+0.8pp
Ravi: seeing the snapshot — +0.8pp is notable but below our absolute alert. still worth paging on high-risk slices (auth, upload).
Kevin: UX question: should the console show guard evaluation logs per deployment? e.g., which guard triggered/fell short, p-values, bootstrap samples.
Olivia: yes, auditability matters for root cause. show evaluated metrics, the rule that fired (or not), and a 'why not alerted' explanation.
Maya: small mock: "Guards evaluated: absolute(>1%), relative(>30%, p<0.05, min_n=500) — result: relative=12% (p=0.03) min_n satisfied -> partial match: flag=true, alert=false (no absolute). Recommend: surface 'partial matches' as a yellow card with suggested actions (increase canary %, rollback, or wait).
Kevin: I like the yellow card. Also add auto-actions for enterprise customers (auto-fallback to baseline if critical slices hit thresholds).
Ravi: operational concern: we need the evaluation to run in near-real-time without adding big read pressure on TSDB. maybe run sampling and incremental counters in the rollout runtime and push a pre-aggregated delta stream to signal service.
Maya: agree — implement streaming deltas per route and slice from the runtime. signal-service will compute p-values and decide guard state.
Olivia: for dashboard drilldown UX: add a "pin slice" feature so an owner can pin sensitive slices (auth, billing) and get priority alerts and historical trends across rollouts.
Kevin: who wants to own a short RFC? I'll draft the alert DSL changes and runtime delta API. Maya take UX for the yellow/partial-card, Olivia you own slice explorer enhancements. Ravi you own signal-service perf constraints.
Maya: assigned. I'll drop sketches in #design after lunch and link a Figma frame.
deploy-bot: Deployment canary-v2 started at 2026-03-18T12:10:10Z (traffic 20%)
Olivia: quick note — add a test harness to replay historical rollouts against the new guard heuristics so we can calibrate false positives/negatives. we can use last 6 months of rollout data.
Ravi: good call. We'll need a synthetic traffic generator for specific slices too.
Maya: ok, thanks all. I'll follow up with PRs and a timeline. :thumbsup:
Kevin: thanks — let's aim to have RFC + basic eval pipeline in 2 sprints.
Olivia: +1
Ravi: +1
signal-bot: [automated] Guard-eval task created: task/GE-4823
Maya: filing follow-ups in the thread and tagging owners.
